clue.text: Trees start to topple after shouts of warning

indicators.note: the letter taken from topple is placed after the golfers' warnings

parts.note: golfers shout 'fore' to warn others of a flying ball

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word topple is all that is wanted here

explanation.surface: A woodsman yells warnings just before a felled tree starts to come down.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the golfer's warning cry; the plural gives FORES, then T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A large area of land covered by trees is called a woodland of this kind; the trees stand for the whole.

clue.text: Money? Penny needs this for a bike

definitions.meaning: an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny

definitions.text: Penny needs this for a bike
definitions.meaning: the Victorian high-wheeled bicycle is named penny-____, after a big and a small coin

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a bike purchase needs extra cash beyond a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: The penny-farthing was a Victorian bicycle with a huge front wheel and tiny rear one, named after two British coins of very different sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a pre-1971 British coin of minimal value, so it is a piece of money; it also completes the bicycle's name.

clue.text: Search through lost file under bottom of drawer

indicators.note: in a down clue the shuffled letters sit beneath the single letter
in a down answer the bottom of a word is its final letter, here of drawer
a lost file is in disarray, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone rummages for a missing document beneath the bottom of a drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' turns FILE into IFLE, placed 'under' R, the last letter of 'drawer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack or rummage through something is a synonym of searching it thoroughly.

clue.text: Agitate about right sort of cup

indicators.note: the phrase for agitating goes around the letter for right

parts.note: to agitate is to stir up

explanation.surface: Someone stirs a drink while musing on what the proper kind of cup is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts STIR UP around R. A stirrup cup is a drink offered to a rider already mounted, before a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup cup is a traditional parting drink, so the word names a particular kind of cup.

clue.text: Invariably left road after a second

indicators.note: the left-and-road pieces come after the letter from a

parts.note: a way is a road or path

explanation.surface: A driver always turns left onto the road a second later than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then L and WAY, then S for second.
explanation.definitionFit: Invariably means at every time without exception, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Reveal changes around hotel in port

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the hotel letter
the word reveal changes its order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' makes LEAVRE from REVEAL, and 'around' places it about H. Le Havre is a major French port on the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Havre is a large French seaport at the mouth of the Seine, an example of a harbour city.

clue.text: Warning light on rigs designed to identify whale product

parts.note: the amber traffic light warns that red is coming

indicators.note: the letters of rigs are designed into a new form

explanation.surface: A warning light on oil rigs is designed to spot whales and their products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' looks like part of the oil-rig picture, but it is the anagram signal. Ambergris, found in sperm whales, was prized in perfume-making.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy substance from sperm whales' intestines, prized in perfumery, so it is a cetacean product.

clue.text: Pooh-poohs ship with cargo of cereal

indicators.note: a ship carrying a cargo holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
corn is a cereal crop

explanation.surface: A merchant dismisses a vessel carrying a load of grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with cargo of' is the container signal: a ship holds its cargo. SS is the steamship prefix on ship names.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh something is to dismiss it with contempt, a close synonym of disdaining it.

clue.text: Good service, appropriate with one style of artwork

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
fit means suitable or appropriate
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Praise for a well-run service that suits a particular art style.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF is the Royal Air Force, one of the British armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: Street art sprayed or scrawled on walls is a recognised style of artwork, often painted illegally.

clue.text: Main lectern possibly raised by degrees

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: The main lectern in a church might be lifted a little at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges MAIN LECTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something increasing in small steps grows gradually, by stages, which describes a step-by-step rise.

clue.text: Rub shoulders with vagrant pinching new book

indicators.note: pinching means taking hold of, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: a hobo is an American word for a vagrant

explanation.surface: A tramp mingles with others while stealing a new book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' puts N inside HOBO, giving HOBNO, then B follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To socialise familiarly with important people is the sense of both phrases, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Assuming he expected to pack butter

indicators.note: the phrase packs the answer inside it, spanning several words

explanation.surface: Someone assumes a man is supposed to pack the butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pack' signals the letters within 'assuminG HE Expected'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is clarified butter used in South Asian cooking, a kind of butter.

clue.text: Getting better engineers and providing insurance

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
covering something is providing insurance for it

explanation.surface: An engineering firm recovers financially while offering insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Recuperating from illness means improving in health, a synonym of getting better.

clue.text: Nice word for a risker of capital

definitions.text: Nice word for a risker of capital

parts.words: Nice word for a risker of capital
parts.note: Nice is the French city, so a 'Nice word' is a French one; the French term for a business risk-taker is borrowed into English

explanation.surface: A polite euphemism for someone who gambles with money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like 'pleasant', but read it as the French city: the word is French in origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A business founder who risks money on a venture is described by this French-derived term.

clue.text: Swine angry over port

parts.note: a swine is a contemptible person, a rotter

indicators.note: in a down answer over means turned upside down, so the word for angry is read backwards

parts.note: mad means angry

explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam, in the Netherlands, is one of the largest seaports in Europe, an example of a harbour city.

clue.text: Idiots featuring on top paper

parts.note: fools are idiots
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

explanation.surface: Fools are featured on top-quality paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Foolscap is an old British paper size, named for a jester's cap watermark.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolscap is a size of writing or printing paper, so the answer is a kind of paper.

clue.text: Single-mindedness of worried vet on insulin

indicators.note: letters that are worried are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet anxious about an animal on insulin focuses on nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges VET ON INSULIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow focus that ignores everything else is figurative single-mindedness, an idiomatic match.

clue.text: Topless dance in exotic sun shades

indicators.note: the cut-down dance goes in among the shuffled letters
exotic signals the letters of sun are made unfamiliar by rearranging
topless means losing the top, the first letter of dance

explanation.surface: A topless dancer performs in the tropical sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' beheads the dance; 'exotic' scrambles sun to NUS; 'in' sets the beheaded dance between NU and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtle gradations of colour or meaning are called shades, a direct synonym of these distinctions.

clue.text: Funny feeling that flipping blog, it reviews shows

explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' gives OGITREV within 'blOG IT REViews'; 'flipping' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizziness, especially a spinning sensation at heights, is a strange physical sensation, colloquially a funny feeling.

clue.text: Bans volunteers with drink, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the combined phrase is heard

parts.note: the TA, the Territorial Army, are reserve volunteers, and booze is drink

explanation.surface: Volunteers are banned from drinking, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's volunteer reserve force; TA plus BOOZE, said aloud, matches the answer.

clue.text: Married constituent imbibing beer is a villain

ale is beer

explanation.walkthrough: L for learner is the plate on British learner drivers' cars; two of them make students.

clue.text: Casual labourer at first needs help and support

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.walkthrough: 'Casual labourer' reads as a phrase, but 'Casual' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed and easy-going describes a casual manner, a synonym.

clue.text: Indian grub from area on Greek island

parts.note: Samos is an island in the Aegean

explanation.surface: Indian food from a district on a Greek island.

clue.text: Carry out survey going back for a measure
